evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/ai-chat/components/ChatInterface.tsx:93-118 - handleSendMessage's no-active-session branch creates the session, calls setCurrentSessionId(session.id), then defers the actual send inside a hardcoded setTimeout(async () => { await sendMessage.mutateAsync({ content }) }, 100). The send mutation is bound to the session id at hook-call time: sendMessage = useSendMessage(currentSessionId || '') (:48), and useSendMessage bakes the id straight into the request URL - useAiChat.ts:97-107 POSTs to `${API_BASE}/sessions/${sessionId}/messages`. The 100ms delay is a magic-number bet that React re-renders and TanStack's MutationObserver picks up the new mutationFn (bound to the fresh session id) before the timer fires; the author flagged the fragility inline: 'This is a simplified version - in production you'd want better state management' (:104).

The deferred send escapes error handling entirely. The outer try/catch (:97-110) wraps only createSession.mutateAsync; the setTimeout callback is a SEPARATE async function whose awaited sendMessage.mutateAsync rejection is caught by nothing - it is an unhandled promise rejection. (The rendered error banner at :254 reads the current-render sendMessage.isError, so whether it lights up depends on MutationObserver identity/timing, not on the setTimeout path handling the error.) On a slow render or a rejected first send, the user's very first message is silently dropped or misrouted with no reliable feedback.

Reachability: AiChatPage.tsx:12 mounts <ChatInterface showSidebar={true}/> with no initialSessionId, so currentSessionId starts null (:36) and EVERY first interaction - typing in ChatInput or clicking a SuggestedQuestions prompt (handleSuggestedQuestion -> handleSendMessage, :122-127) - takes this no-session branch. This is the primary entry point of the AI chat feature (Epic 127), not an edge path.

Fix (low-risk, removes the race): thread the freshly-created session id through explicitly instead of relying on state + a timer - e.g. capture const newId = session.id and call a send bound to newId (either useSendMessage refactored to take the id as a mutate argument, or await sendMessage.mutateAsync({ sessionId: newId, content })), all inside the same try/catch so a failed first send surfaces to the user. Drop the setTimeout entirely.
